notes.title: Ongoing Update - Mid June
notes.content:
With the first weeks of release past, and the first major update, we continue to follow-up players remarks and various comments on the game, improving it as they come.


Today's changes:


Data: some Korean characters names were poorly written and have been changed following players remarks (change)

Data: Korean boats are properly name (no more 'Junks')

Graphics: Kamons of 1st and 8th divisions were inverted (fix).

Gameplay : mostly for play balance, mainly in the field of logisitcs and naval combat.

unsupplied militias will suffer more hits and vanish more quickly

Japanese 1st and 2nd divisions will do more looting on their initial turns (turn 1-24), allowing them to recruit more supply units

some of the large Bune ships have been strengthened (resitance and firepower)

Japanese naval commanders re-assigned more accurately

notes.title: SGS IMJIN WAR FIRST POST-RELEASE UPDATE
notes.content:
Based on continued playtest and initial remarks of our customers, we have prepared our first post-release update, with the following new elements or actions

NEW CONTENT
- Added many new units for Ming China, among which

 	Guards for Beijing
 	Frontier Troops
 	Elite Arquebusier
 	Grand General canon
 	Culverine light field gun
 	New Wei yuan pao gun-mortar
 	Fujian heavy warship

- Added new events such as

 	Maritime Trade events (for both side)
 	Firearms purchase (Joeson can purchase firearms troops only after Ming intervention


FIXED, IMPROVED OR ALTERED CONTENT
- Changed some data that prevent generals to properly command in battle
- Changed combat values and/or life points of some units (Atakebune, Samurai Ashigarus, Ming Heavy Cavalry, some Jurchens)
- Changed picture of general Li Rusong to better reflect his age at time of this war
- Improved morale values of some units (e.g. Ming infantry morale increased by 1)
- Overall revision and change of all leaders in the game (to give a better balance, for both sides)
- Re-assigned one region that was wrongly in Chungcheong to Gyeongsang province.
- Forbid some strange Jurchens units placement.
- Full revision of the Chinese language version (proofread by native Chinese wargamer).

Special thanks to our friend Wang Wenqi who, in addition to Chinese language proofreading,  provided us good information on Ming China (and access to the book “A Dragon’s Head and a Serpent’s Tail” which gives a lot of verified points on Ming art of war).
